rv.q: If this rambunctious comedy had its tongue any more firmly planted in its cheek, surgery would be required to remove it.
If there are some well-acted, genuinely poignant scenes, the show is at heart sketch comedy, mixing pointed parody with silly slapstick, and unafraid to be sophomoric, even when depicting atrocities.
Between Two Knees is a noble effort to tell the story of one hundred years of Native American suffering through the Lakota tribe, but it seems to want to cover too much in too parodistic a style.
It's a numbing, scattershot evening that alternatively wants to amuse us and slap us around.
Between Two Knees is the kind of show you laugh at politely, hoping that will somehow expedite its conclusion.
Between Two Knees hits its targets with impressive regularity.
White people receive quite a spanking in the New York premiere of the 1491s’ irreverent, hilarious, and scattershot theatrical history lesson, Between Two Knees.

cn.t: Critics find this indigenous sketch comedy troupe's epic historical journey from 1890 to 1973 irreverent and ambitious, but opinions split on whether its mix of bawdy humor and poignant moments successfully balances comedy with its serious subject matter.
